bounded_statement: The report's selected result — a two-sample Student t-test giving t(58) = 26.40, p < 0.0001 for rewetted vs drained CH4 flux — is computed on all 60 chamber readings as if each were an independent observation, but the declared independent unit is plot_id and there are only 12 plots (6 per regime), each contributing 5 repeated seasonal readings. The reported degrees of freedom (58 rather than 10), t-statistic, and p-value are therefore not supported by the design; only the mean difference of 6.00 mg m-2 h-1 is a design-agnostic summary, and any significance claim requires a plot-level or mixed-model reanalysis.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report is transparent that the test was run on individual readings rather than concealing the unit of analysis, and the between-regime separation (means 4.25 vs 10.25 with per-plot means well separated) is so large that a correct plot-level analysis on 6 vs 6 plot means would very likely remain significant in the same direction. This mitigates the practical consequence but does not make the reported t(58), n = 60, or p-value valid.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: Report openly states the 60-reading basis; plot means do not overlap between regimes (drained about 3.0-5.5, rewetted about 9.0-11.5)

source_refs.quoted_text:
During the 2024 growing season a field crew visited every plot five
times. On each visit a static closed chamber was seated on the plot
collar, the headspace was sampled over half an hour, and the resulting
methane flux was written down together with the air temperature inside
the chamber. Twelve plots visited five times each gives 60 lines in the
table.

- plot_id: label of the permanent monitoring plot (DR-01 to DR-06 in the
  drained sector, RW-01 to RW-06 in the rewetted sector); the same plot
  reappears once per survey round

One row is: one static-chamber methane flux measurement taken on one monitoring plot during one of the five seasonal survey rounds
Independent unit column: plot_id

evidence.description: The workflow pools flux values by regime only, ignoring plot_id entirely, so all five repeated readings from each plot enter the pooled sample as separate values.
evidence.observed_value: flux_samples() keys only on water_table_regime; plot_id is never referenced in the analysis

evidence.description: The pooled per-row arrays are passed directly to scipy.stats.ttest_ind, a procedure that assumes every element is an independent observation, and degrees of freedom are computed from row counts (30+30-2=58) rather than plot counts (6+6-2=10).
evidence.observed_value: ttest_ind on 30-row arrays; df = n_rw + n_dr - 2 = 58

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify the finding by searching the workflow for any step that aggregates or models the repeated measurements at the plot level before inference: flux_samples() is the only grouping step and it keys solely on water_table_regime, plot_id appears nowhere in analysis.py outside the raw DictReader rows, and no per-plot averaging, mixed model, or cluster-robust adjustment exists. I also checked whether the report's claim could be read as plot-level: it cannot, since it explicitly cites the 60 individual chamber readings and t(58), and the summary table reports 30 measurements per regime rather than 6 plots. I verified the arithmetic is consistent with row-level pooling (30 rows per regime, df = 30 + 30 - 2 = 58). Finally, I checked whether the rows could plausibly be independent despite the description: the data show tight within-plot clustering across survey rounds, contradicting row independence. No reading of the files avoids the conclusion.

root_cause: The workflow's flux_samples() function pools rows by water_table_regime alone and never uses plot_id, so each plot's five repeated survey-round measurements enter scipy.stats.ttest_ind as five separate observations; the row-independent t-test then treats n as 30 rows per regime instead of 6 plots per regime, inflating degrees of freedom from 10 to 58 and understating the standard error of the group means.
